question: If the diagonal of a rhombus are 15 cm and 24 cm, then its area will be.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The area of a rhombus is half the product of its diagonals.

Area = ½ × d₁ × d₂

Area = ½ × 15 × 24

Area = 15 × 12 = 180 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 180 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Rhombus

All four sides of a rhombus are equal in length, and opposite sides are parallel to each other.

Diagonals Relationship

The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles (90°).

Side and Diagonal Formula

The relationship between the side (a) and diagonals (d₁, d₂) is given by: 4a² = d₁² + d₂².

Perimeter of Rhombus

The perimeter of a rhombus is the total length of its boundaries, calculated as: P = 4 × a.
